text: Sustainable management of resources using science-based information

sources.sourceText: 1. Sustainable management of resources using science-based information

activities:
Ensure sustainable management of the living marine resources based on the best available evidence from social, economic and ecological sciences.
Apply ecosystem and precautionary approaches to promote responsible fisheries management.
Enhance the stocks of endangered, threatened and protected species.
Enhance fish stocks in the territorial sea and the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) by ranching and habitat enhancement.
Prevent overcapacity of the fishing fleet.
Divert marine fishing efforts from over-exploited areas to unexploited or under- exploited areas.
Promote the use of fishing practices and equipment that cause comparatively low adverse impacts on the environment.
Maintain the ban of fishing in Sri Lanka waters by foreign fishing vessels except for research and development purposes.
Promote responsible fisheries in compliance with requirements stipulated in international treaties concerning management of fisheries.
Limit the new access to high seas fishing only to fishing vessels equipped with state- of-the-art technology for fish detection, on-board fish quality maintenance, etc.
Apply ecosystem approach to management of fisheries in inland waters.
Ensure conservation of aquatic biodiversity in inland waters.
Regulate the length and engine capacity of fishing vessel fishing in lagoons and estuaries.
Not allow the use of motorized boats for fishing in reservoirs.
Apply temporal and spatial planning in development of aquaculture.
Allocate land and water resources for aquaculture projects only after environmental, socio-economic and cultural impact assessments.
Ensure that aquaculture projects are implemented in strict compliance with conditions of approval.
Strengthen the aquaculture-animal healthcare activities.
Promote the use of best management practices (BMPs) in aquaculture.
